paragraphs.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called [to be] an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,
paragraphs.original: Παῦλος δοῦλος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, κλητὸς ἀπόστολος, ἀφωρισμένος εἰς εὐαγγέλιον θεοῦ
paragraphs.translit: Paulos doulos Christou Iēsou, klētos apostolos, aphōrismenos eis euangelion theou

paragraphs.text: which he promised afore through his prophets in the holy scriptures,
paragraphs.original: ὃ προεπηγγείλατο διὰ τῶν προφητῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν γραφαῖς ἁγίαις
paragraphs.translit: ho proepēngeilato dia tōn prophētōn autou en graphais hagiais

paragraphs.text: concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,
paragraphs.original: περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ γενομένου ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ κατὰ σάρκα,
paragraphs.translit: peri tou hyiou autou, tou genomenou ek spermatos Dauid kata sarka,

paragraphs.text: who was declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead; [even] Jesus Christ our Lord,
paragraphs.original: τοῦ ὁρισθέντος υἱοῦ θεοῦ ἐν δυνάμει κατὰ πνεῦμα ἁγιωσύνης ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: tou horisthentos hyiou theou en dynamei kata pneuma hagiōsynēs ex anastaseōs nekrōn, Iēsou Christou tou kyriou hēmōn,

paragraphs.text: through whom we received grace and apostleship, unto obedience of faith among all the nations, for his name`s sake;
paragraphs.original: διʼ οὗ ἐλάβομεν χάριν καὶ ἀποστολὴν εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: diʼ hou elabomen charin kai apostolēn eis hypakoēn pisteōs en pasin tois ethnesin hyper tou onomatos autou,

paragraphs.text: among whom are ye also called [to be] Jesus Christ`s:
paragraphs.original: ἐν οἷς ἐστε καὶ ὑμεῖς κλητοὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: en hois este kai hymeis klētoi Iēsou Christou,

paragraphs.text: To all that are in Rome, beloved of God, called [to be] saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
paragraphs.original: πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Ῥώμῃ ἀγαπητοῖς θεοῦ, κλητοῖς ἁγίοις· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: pasin tois ousin en Rhōmē agapētois theou, klētois hagiois· charis hymin kai eirēnē apo theou patros hēmōn kai kyriou Iēsou Christou.

paragraphs.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.
paragraphs.original: Πρῶτον μὲν εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καταγγέλλεται ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ.
paragraphs.translit: Prōton men eucharistō tō theō mou dia Iēsou Christou peri pantōn hymōn, hoti hē pistis hymōn katangelletai en holō tō kosmō.

paragraphs.text: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you, always in my prayers
paragraphs.original: μάρτυς γάρ μού ἐστιν ὁ θεός, ᾧ λατρεύω ἐν τῷ πνεύματί μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἀδιαλείπτως μνείαν ὑμῶν ποιοῦμαι
paragraphs.translit: martys gar mou estin ho theos, hō latreuō en tō pneumati mou en tō euangeliō tou hyiou autou, hōs adialeiptōs mneian hymōn poioumai

paragraphs.text: making request, if by any means now at length I may be prospered by the will of God to come unto you.
paragraphs.original: πάντοτε ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου, δεόμενος εἴ πως ἤδη ποτὲ εὐοδωθήσομαι ἐν τῷ θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: pantote epi tōn proseuchōn mou, deomenos ei pōs ēdē pote euodōthēsomai en tō thelēmati tou theou elthein pros hymas.

paragraphs.text: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;
paragraphs.original: ἐπιποθῶ γὰρ ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἵνα τι μεταδῶ χάρισμα ὑμῖν πνευματικὸν εἰς τὸ στηριχθῆναι ὑμᾶς,
paragraphs.translit: epipothō gar idein hymas, hina ti metadō charisma hymin pneumatikon eis to stērichthēnai hymas,

paragraphs.text: that is, that I with you may be comforted in you, each of us by the other`s faith, both yours and mine.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν συμπαρακληθῆναι ἐν ὑμῖν διὰ τῆς ἐν ἀλλήλοις πίστεως ὑμῶν τε καὶ ἐμοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: touto de estin symparaklēthēnai en hymin dia tēs en allēlois pisteōs hymōn te kai emou.

paragraphs.text: And I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you (and was hindered hitherto), that I might have some fruit in you also, even as in the rest of the Gentiles.
paragraphs.original: οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι πολλάκις προεθέμην ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἐκωλύθην ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, ἵνα τινὰ καρπὸν σχῶ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς καὶ ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ou thelō de hymas agnoein, adelphoi, hoti pollakis proethemēn elthein pros hymas, kai ekōlythēn achri tou deuro, hina tina karpon schō kai en hymin kathōs kai en tois loipois ethnesin.

paragraphs.text: I am debtor both to Greeks and to Barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish.
paragraphs.original: Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις, σοφοῖς τε καὶ ἀνοήτοις ὀφειλέτης εἰμί·
paragraphs.translit: Hellēsin te kai barbarois, sophois te kai anoētois opheiletēs eimi·

paragraphs.text: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you also that are in Rome.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως τὸ κατʼ ἐμὲ πρόθυμον καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐν Ῥώμῃ εὐαγγελίσασθαι.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs to katʼ eme prothymon kai hymin tois en Rhōmē euangelisasthai.

paragraphs.text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
paragraphs.original: Οὐ γὰρ ἐπαισχύνομαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, δύναμις γὰρ θεοῦ ἐστιν εἰς σωτηρίαν παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι·
paragraphs.translit: Ou gar epaischynomai to euangelion, dynamis gar theou estin eis sōtērian panti tō pisteuonti, Ioudaiō te prōton kai Hellēni·

paragraphs.text: For therein is revealed a righteousness of God from faith unto faith: as it is written, But the righteous shall live by faith.
paragraphs.original: δικαιοσύνη γὰρ θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν, καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: dikaiosynē gar theou en autō apokalyptetai ek pisteōs eis pistin, kathōs gegraptai· Ho de dikaios ek pisteōs zēsetai.

paragraphs.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hinder the truth in unrighteousness;
paragraphs.original: Ἀποκαλύπτεται γὰρ ὀργὴ θεοῦ ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ἀσέβειαν καὶ ἀδικίαν ἀνθρώπων τῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐν ἀδικίᾳ κατεχόντων,
paragraphs.translit: Apokalyptetai gar orgē theou apʼ ouranou epi pasan asebeian kai adikian anthrōpōn tōn tēn alētheian en adikia katechontōn,

paragraphs.text: because that which is known of God is manifest in them; for God manifested it unto them.
paragraphs.original: διότι τὸ γνωστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φανερόν ἐστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς, ὁ θεὸς γὰρ αὐτοῖς ἐφανέρωσεν.
paragraphs.translit: dioti to gnōston tou theou phaneron estin en autois, ho theos gar autois ephanerōsen.

paragraphs.text: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, [even] his everlasting power and divinity; that they may be without excuse:
paragraphs.original: τὰ γὰρ ἀόρατα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου τοῖς ποιήμασιν νοούμενα καθορᾶται, ἥ τε ἀΐδιος αὐτοῦ δύναμις καὶ θειότης, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἀναπολογήτους,
paragraphs.translit: ta gar aorata autou apo ktiseōs kosmou tois poiēmasin nooumena kathoratai, hē te aidios autou dynamis kai theiotēs, eis to einai autous anapologētous,

paragraphs.text: because that, knowing God, they glorified him not as God, neither gave thanks; but became vain in their reasonings, and their senseless heart was darkened.
paragraphs.original: διότι γνόντες τὸν θεὸν οὐχ ὡς θεὸν ἐδόξασαν ἢ ηὐχαρίστησαν, ἀλλὰ ἐματαιώθησαν ἐν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία·
paragraphs.translit: dioti gnontes ton theon ouch hōs theon edoxasan ē ēucharistēsan, alla emataiōthēsan en tois dialogismois autōn kai eskotisthē hē asynetos autōn kardia·

paragraphs.text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
paragraphs.original: φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ ἐμωράνθησαν,
paragraphs.translit: phaskontes einai sophoi emōranthēsan,

paragraphs.text: and changed the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and four-footed beasts, and creeping things.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ ἀφθάρτου θεοῦ ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος φθαρτοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πετεινῶν καὶ τετραπόδων καὶ ἑρπετῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēllaxan tēn doxan tou aphthartou theou en homoiōmati eikonos phthartou anthrōpou kai peteinōn kai tetrapodōn kai herpetōn.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts unto uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves:
paragraphs.original: Διὸ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῶν καρδιῶν αὐτῶν εἰς ἀκαθαρσίαν τοῦ ἀτιμάζεσθαι τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς,
paragraphs.translit: Dio paredōken autous ho theos en tais epithymiais tōn kardiōn autōn eis akatharsian tou atimazesthai ta sōmata autōn en autois,

paragraphs.text: for that they exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshipped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.
paragraphs.original: οἵτινες μετήλλαξαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ψεύδει, καὶ ἐσεβάσθησαν καὶ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα, ὅς ἐστιν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
paragraphs.translit: hoitines metēllaxan tēn alētheian tou theou en tō pseudei, kai esebasthēsan kai elatreusan tē ktisei para ton ktisanta, hos estin eulogētos eis tous aiōnas· amēn.

paragraphs.text: For this cause God gave them up unto vile passions: for their women changed the natural use into that which is against nature:
paragraphs.original: Διὰ τοῦτο παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς πάθη ἀτιμίας· αἵ τε γὰρ θήλειαι αὐτῶν μετήλλαξαν τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν εἰς τὴν παρὰ φύσιν,
paragraphs.translit: Dia touto paredōken autous ho theos eis pathē atimias· hai te gar thēleiai autōn metēllaxan tēn physikēn chrēsin eis tēn para physin,

paragraphs.text: and likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another, men with men working unseemliness, and receiving in themselves that recompense of their error which was due.
paragraphs.original: ὁμοίως τε καὶ οἱ ἄρσενες ἀφέντες τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν τῆς θηλείας ἐξεκαύθησαν ἐν τῇ ὀρέξει αὐτῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους, ἄρσενες ἐν ἄρσεσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην κατεργαζόμενοι καὶ τὴν ἀντιμισθίαν ἣν ἔδει τῆς πλάνης αὐτῶν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀπολαμβάνοντες.
paragraphs.translit: homoiōs te kai hoi arsenes aphentes tēn physikēn chrēsin tēs thēleias exekauthēsan en tē orexei autōn eis allēlous, arsenes en arsesin tēn aschēmosynēn katergazomenoi kai tēn antimisthian hēn edei tēs planēs autōn en heautois apolambanontes.

paragraphs.text: And even as they refused to have God in [their] knowledge, God gave them up unto a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ καθὼς οὐκ ἐδοκίμασαν τὸν θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἐπιγνώσει, παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς ἀδόκιμον νοῦν, ποιεῖν τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα,
paragraphs.translit: Kai kathōs ouk edokimasan ton theon echein en epignōsei, paredōken autous ho theos eis adokimon noun, poiein ta mē kathēkonta,

paragraphs.text: being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malignity; whisperers,
paragraphs.original: πεπληρωμένους πάσῃ ἀδικίᾳ πονηρίᾳ πλεονεξίᾳ κακίᾳ, μεστοὺς φθόνου φόνου ἔριδος δόλου κακοηθείας, ψιθυριστάς,
paragraphs.translit: peplērōmenous pasē adikia ponēria pleonexia kakia, mestous phthonou phonou eridos dolou kakoētheias, psithyristas,

paragraphs.text: backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, haughty, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
paragraphs.original: καταλάλους, θεοστυγεῖς, ὑβριστάς, ὑπερηφάνους, ἀλαζόνας, ἐφευρετὰς κακῶν, γονεῦσιν ἀπειθεῖς,
paragraphs.translit: katalalous, theostygeis, hybristas, hyperēphanous, alazonas, epheuretas kakōn, goneusin apeitheis,

paragraphs.text: without understanding, covenant-breakers, without natural affection, unmerciful:
paragraphs.original: ἀσυνέτους, ἀσυνθέτους, ἀστόργους, ἀνελεήμονας·
paragraphs.translit: asynetous, asynthetous, astorgous, aneleēmonas·

paragraphs.text: who, knowing the ordinance of God, that they that practise such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also consent with them that practise them.
paragraphs.original: οἵτινες τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπιγνόντες, ὅτι οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντες ἄξιοι θανάτου εἰσίν, οὐ μόνον αὐτὰ ποιοῦσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ συνευδοκοῦσιν τοῖς πράσσουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hoitines to dikaiōma tou theou epignontes, hoti hoi ta toiauta prassontes axioi thanatou eisin, ou monon auta poiousin alla kai syneudokousin tois prassousin.
